subject: variational surrogate
statement: The paper presents an analytically grounded variational surrogate framework in which a shallow Variational Quantum Circuit (VQC) is trained to reproduce the QPE measurement distribution without any quantum circuit simulation.

subject: QPE on NISQ hardware
statement: The paper eliminates the exponentially scaling simulation bottleneck of prior surrogate approaches by computing the training target entirely classically via the Dirichlet kernel.

subject: R_Y-R_Z-CZ ansatz optimization
statement: Comparing linear and full entangler topologies for the R_Y-R_Z-CZ ansatz on IBM Quantum hardware, the paper identifies the linear entangler as optimal across four distributional metrics.

subject: VQC depth on noisy hardware
statement: For the linear-entangler ansatz, the paper identifies single-layer depth as optimal under hardware noise.

subject: ground-state energy estimation
statement: The paper recovers the ground-state energy of the hydrogen molecule within the chemical accuracy threshold (1 kcal/mol) using a linearly scaling VQC on IBM Quantum hardware.

subject: Grievance Dictionary evaluation
statement: On a non-circular evaluation pool, the paper shows the Grievance Dictionary's apparent macro-AUROC of 0.686 collapses to a 0.500 floor fixed by construction due to lexicon-driven selection bias.

subject: contextual models for grievance
statement: The paper proposes replacing word-level term matching with context-reading models to better resolve whether terms are asserted, quoted, negated, or condemned.

subject: post context in grievance detection
statement: Reading the full post rather than the target sentence alone raises average precision on lexicon-negative text from 0.14 to 0.20, with largest gains on quoted and implicit grievance.

subject: multilingual grievance benchmark
statement: The paper releases code and benchmark at https://github.com/behavioral-ds/multilingual_grievance.

subject: Best-of-Evidence selection
statement: The paper introduces Best-of-Evidence (BoE), an inference-time selection framework that keeps the BoN candidate pool fixed and allocates a limited budget to evidence actions under partial verification.

subject: evidence capacity in selection
statement: The paper shows theoretically that residual evidence capacity limits any evidence-driven improvement in fixed-pool selection.

subject: factor queries in selection
statement: In a factor-code model, the paper shows shared factor queries can achieve an O(log K) versus Θ(K) query separation.

subject: medical VQA with partial evidence
statement: Common-ledger experiments on four medical VQA settings show that BoE can improve fixed-pool selection when evidence is reliable, contrastive, and decision-relevant.

subject: latent reasoning in chess
statement: The paper finds that latent reasoning does not function as an actively consulted inference-time scratchpad, but instead shapes model parameters during training.

subject: RL robustness in latent reasoning
statement: Under RL training, the paper shows latent reasoning adds robustness to disruption of latent thought vectors rather than reliance on thought content.

subject: chess legality with RL
statement: The paper reports legality in chess play climbs monotonically to 61% after RL training, from a 48% pre-RL baseline.

subject: checkmate in chess
statement: The paper shows checkmate confabulation is eliminated entirely by RL training.

subject: kNNG on BGE-M3 embeddings
statement: The paper utilizes Equi-Voronoi Polytopes (EVP) for efficient quantization in k-Nearest Neighbor Graph construction on 1024-dimensional BGE-M3 embeddings.

subject: ANNS query latency optimization
statement: The paper introduces a 1D presorting mechanism via Fast Linear Assignment Sorting (FLAS) prior to graph construction, significantly improving spatial locality and cache hit rates.

subject: MIPS with dimensionality augmentation
statement: For Maximum Inner Product Search (MIPS), the paper transforms the asymmetric inner product problem into a Euclidean search space via dimensionality augmentation.

subject: ANNS indexing challenge
statement: The paper releases source code at https://github.com/Visual-Computing/sisap26-deglib.

subject: sequence-level INR supervision
statement: The paper reformulates implicit neural representations (INRs) for time-varying volumetric data as a collection of spatially indexed time series with sequence-level supervision.

subject: INR training efficiency
statement: Sequence-level supervision eliminates the need for dense spatiotemporal sampling and significantly reduces training cost while improving reconstruction quality.

subject: INR architectural compatibility
statement: The paper demonstrates that sequence-level supervision is compatible with a range of existing INR architectures.

subject: MoE-based INR variants
statement: The paper shows mixture-of-experts instantiation of the sequence-level INR formulation further improves reconstruction quality compared to both base reformulation and existing MoE-based INR methods.

subject: cue-anchored memory for agents
statement: The paper proposes a cue-anchored memory model where memories carry first-class trigger conditions over a composable vocabulary (path, symbol, semantic, event, temporal) evaluated deterministically by the harness.

subject: voluntary memory in agents
statement: Controlled evaluation shows voluntary memory use is near zero even with a pre-seeded store, with 0 memory operations in 114 turns.

subject: deterministic memory injection
statement: The paper shows deterministic injection of cue-anchored memories is delivered in every seeded run with zero false alarms.

subject: memory persistence in compaction
statement: The paper shows 39% of intra-session re-reads re-buy content paid for before a compaction boundary, indicating selective value.

subject: visual token compression effects
statement: The paper finds that visual token compression alters downstream feature distributions and affects MoE routing decisions in multimodal models.

subject: MoE routing interactions
statement: The paper identifies that routing behavior affects expert utilization and quantization sensitivity in multimodal edge inference.

subject: multimodal optimization coupling
statement: The paper argues that visual token compression, routing, and quantization techniques cannot be treated as independent optimizations in multimodal edge intelligence.

subject: GuardianAgentBench
statement: The paper presents GuardianAgentBench (GABench), a benchmark of 580 scenarios across six domains evaluated on LangChain, LlamaIndex, and Vectara frameworks.

subject: LLM agent reliability
statement: Experiments reveal that even the strongest configuration achieves only 74.8% overall accuracy, with stronger models under-calling required tools and weaker models mis-selecting and over-calling.

subject: agent performance degradation
statement: The paper shows performance degrades monotonically with both tool-set size and sequential turn depth, with long-horizon planning as the steeper bottleneck.

subject: guardrails for agent safety
statement: Guardrail implementation consistently outperforms system-prompt-based defenses, recovering 19.9% of failures at a false positive rate of just 0.5%.

subject: hybrid world-VLA framework
statement: The paper proposes HyWorldVLA, a hybrid world-VLA framework that unifies pixel-level supervision and latent representation learning for autonomous driving.

subject: video VAE with pixel grounding
statement: HyWorldVLA predicts video latents encoded by a pre-trained video VAE while simultaneously reconstructing video frames to provide precise pixel-level grounding.

subject: autonomous driving benchmarks
statement: Extensive experiments on NAVSIM v1 and v2 benchmarks demonstrate that HyWorldVLA significantly outperforms both pixel-based and latent-based world model baselines.

subject: world model noise robustness
statement: The paper presents the first comprehensive qualitative and quantitative analysis of world model noise robustness in autonomous driving.

subject: sparse concept channels
statement: The paper shows that each radiological finding is encoded by a sparse set of approximately 10 vision-encoder channels that match full-feature classification performance.

subject: channel ablation in medical VLM
statement: Turning off the channels tied to one radiological finding causes that finding's score to collapse while unrelated labels remain stable.

subject: sparse channels cross-architecture
statement: The same sparse probe replicates on an architecturally unrelated 3D abdominal VLM (Merlin), suggesting a general property of frozen medical encoders.

subject: concept channel probe
statement: The training-free concept channel probe (CCP) method outperforms published CT-CHAT on clinical efficacy (F1 0.549 vs. 0.184) and BLEU (0.483 vs. 0.373) at 22x lower latency.

subject: animacy circuit in LLMs
statement: The paper discovers an animacy circuit, a causal mechanism responsible for handling animacy in large language models through circuit discovery on four open-weight models.

subject: animacy circuit generalization
statement: The paper finds the animacy circuit is less localized compared to other known circuits and generalizes only partially across models and animacy tasks.

subject: animacy minimal pairs dataset
statement: The paper constructs a controlled dataset of minimal pairs for circuit discovery on animacy tasks across four models.

subject: Workflow-Localized Mechanism Learning
statement: The paper introduces Workflow-Localized Mechanism Learning (WML), which jointly resolves failure location, implicated mechanisms, and relevant third-party knowledge reuse for agent skills.

subject: WML on spreadsheet tasks
statement: On SpreadsheetBench, WML reaches 90.33 +/- 1.53% Hard Accuracy with DeepSeek and 74.67 +/- 3.51% with Qwen3.6-Flash.

subject: skill transfer to tables
statement: Without additional optimization, learned Skills transfer to WikiTableQuestions with 84.00 +/- 2.00% Denotation Accuracy (DeepSeek) and 83.00 +/- 2.00% (Qwen3.6-Flash).

subject: WML on compiler tasks
statement: On Compiler-Supported50, WML attains both the highest hard-PASS rate and the lowest cost per successful task.

subject: workflow-guided skill optimization
statement: The paper releases code and artifacts at https://github.com/xiaolin9595/workflow-localized-mechanism-learning.

subject: Naju discrete state-space model
statement: The paper introduces Naju (Native Adaptive Junction Unit), which factorizes the recurrent update into an explicit discrete pole (learned forget gate), independent write gain, and input-dependent maps.

subject: Naju Schur-stability
statement: The paper shows Naju satisfies Schur-stability by construction through sigmoid pole constraint 0 < f_n < 1 and fading-memory bounds.

subject: retention and overwriting trade-off
statement: The paper demonstrates that Naju is the only evaluated model that remains strong on both retention and overwriting at 4x the training length.

subject: Naju language modeling
statement: Naju outperforms Mamba baselines on WikiText-103 language modeling in principal comparisons.

subject: Naju associative recall
statement: The paper shows Naju achieves competitive or superior performance on Long Range Arena and multi-query associative recall tasks.

subject: Naju computational scaling
statement: The paper preserves linear-time, linear-memory scaling with Naju.

subject: ADABORD ordinal classification
statement: The paper introduces ADABORD, an AdaBoost framework specifically designed for ordinal classification with ordinal Gini splitting and ranked probability score error.

subject: ordinal classification benchmark
statement: ADABORD is extensively compared against seven state-of-the-art methods on the TOC-UCO repository, the largest benchmark collection for ordinal classification.

subject: ADABORD on multi-class datasets
statement: Experimental results show ADABORD significantly outperforms competing methods, particularly on datasets with five or more classes.

subject: ADABORD reproducibility
statement: The paper releases source code, experimental protocols, and comparative results publicly for reproducibility.

subject: weight-norm criticality
statement: The paper identifies weight-norm criticality, an additional mechanism for training instability induced by interaction between normalization and weight decay.

subject: scale-invariant weight norms
statement: The paper shows weight decay drives scale-invariant weight norms toward zero, increasing loss landscape sharpness and destabilizing optimization.

subject: weight-norm criticality validation
statement: The paper provides testable predictions of weight-norm criticality validated empirically in networks with scale-invariant components.

subject: LLM-summarizer stability
statement: The paper proposes a two-level diagnostic protocol for benchmarking LLM-summarizers based on stability of generated summaries under controlled conditions.

subject: document-level stability analysis
statement: The paper performs document-level stability analysis over multiple LLM-summaries in controlled environment with semantic and factual alignment scoring.

subject: LLM variability in summarization
statement: Empirical investigation of three LLM-summarizers across three genres reveals statistically significant differences in generation-level variability among LLMs.

subject: EmoAgent-R1 emotion recognition
statement: The paper proposes EmoAgent-R1, a Reinforcement Learning-based Dynamic Agent Specialization framework for multimodal emotion recognition (MER) with dynamic agent routing.

subject: Progressive Group-Relative Policy
statement: The paper introduces Progressive Group-Relative Policy Optimization (P-GRPO) combining group-based relative advantages with PMI-inspired token-level modulation for RL training.

subject: EmoAgent-R1 performance
statement: Extensive experiments demonstrate EmoAgent-R1's superiority in stronger emotion reasoning performance and improved optimization stability on MER benchmarks.

subject: CultureTalk-ID benchmark
statement: The paper introduces CultureTalk-ID, the first dialogue-based benchmark for cultural commonsense in Indonesian and local languages.

subject: multilingual cultural dialogues
statement: CultureTalk-ID comprises 4,496 culturally grounded dialogues across 11 languages and 13 culturally salient topics, curated with native speakers.

subject: cultural commonsense tasks
statement: CultureTalk-ID introduces three complementary tasks: dialogue-based multiple-choice cultural commonsense reasoning, culturally faithful machine translation, and language steering.

subject: HiMe health agent platform
statement: The paper presents HiMe, a locally deployable, privacy-first agent platform fully compatible with real-time health data ecosystems across wearable devices.

subject: personal health agentic analysis
statement: HiMe is guided by three design principles: treating the database as a first-class component, jointly optimizing effectiveness and efficiency, and processing data in real time with long-term user modeling.

subject: continuous health monitoring
statement: The paper enables individuals to harness Personal Health Agents for continuous, personalised health monitoring for better wellbeing through HiMe.
